title: GPU-hour token econ heatmap exploration
summary: Exploratory sensitivity matrix and heatmap-style sheet that maps GPU-hour burn and $/1M tokens across instance families and regions for mid-term capacity planning.
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet is an exploratory tool to answer: given a mix of instance families (A100/RTX6000/GPU-eq), region price spreads, and utilization assumptions, what is the implied GPU-hour burn and $/1M tokens across scenarios? The goal is to identify breakpoints where routing policy should prefer cheaper regions or different instance families, and where Dedicated commitments make sense.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Model mix: 60% generation (variable seq length), 30% chat (latency-sensitive), 10% embeddings/batching.
- Token distribution: median request = 120 tokens input, 300 tokens output for generation; chat = 40 in / 80 out.
- Effective throughput per GPU-hour (baseline perf profile):
  - a100-80GB: 45k tokens/sec sustained aggregate (mixed workloads), 162M tokens/hour
  - rtx-6000-48GB: 22k tokens/sec, 79.2M tokens/hour
  - gpu-eq-light (quantized): 15k tokens/sec, 54M tokens/hour
- Cloud list $/GPU-hour (example):
  - us-east-1 a100-80: $24.00/hr (on-demand), $12.00/hr (reserved blended)
  - europe-west-1 a100-80: $28.00/hr, $14.00/hr reserved
  - us-west-2 rtx-6000: $8.50/hr, $5.50/hr reserved
  - asia-southeast-1 gpu-eq-light: $6.00/hr, $4.00/hr reserved
- Utilization target buckets: low=30%, mid=60%, high=85% (applies to committed pool).
- Overhead & non-token work multiplier: +8% GPU-hour for control plane and I/O overhead.

Key calculated metrics (explicit formulas shown as plain text):
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = tokens_per_sec * 3600 * utilization
- effective_gpu_hour_cost = $/GPU-hour * (1 + overhead)
- $/1M_tokens = effective_gpu_hour_cost / (tokens_per_gpu_hour / 1_000_000)
- implied_token_passthrough = peak-concurrency headroom adjustments (applied as utilization shrinkage under tail-latency SLOs)

Sample scenario table (baseline utilization = 60%):
| region | instance | $/GPUh | tokens/h (raw) | tokens/h (utilized) | effective $/GPUh | $/1M tokens | notes |
us-east-1 | a100-80 | 24.00 | 162,000,000 | 97,200,000 | 25.92 | 0.2668 | baseline high perf
eu-west-1 | a100-80 | 28.00 | 162,000,000 | 97,200,000 | 30.24 | 0.3111 | europe premium
us-west-2 | rtx-6000 | 8.50  | 79,200,000  | 47,520,000  | 9.18  | 0.1932 | lower per-hour cost but half throughput
asia-southeast-1 | gpu-eq-light | 6.00 | 54,000,000 | 32,400,000 | 6.48 | 0.2000 | quantized variant

Observations from example numbers:
- Even though rtx-6000 and gpu-eq-light have lower $/GPUh, their lower token throughput per hour can produce similar or worse $/1M tokens compared to a100 in regions with modest price spreads.
- Europe premium on a100 pushes $/1M above 30c; routing latency-sensitive chat to eu-west1 should be weighed against the incremental cost.
- Quantized variants narrow cost but may introduce quality/regression risk; treat as compatible only for batch/embedding workloads initially.

Sensitivity matrix approach:
- Dimensions: Region price delta (±30%), Utilization (30/60/85%), Model efficiency variance (±20% tokens/sec).
- For each cell compute percent delta in $/1M tokens relative to baseline. Generate heatmap coloring: green < -10% (cheaper), amber between -10% and +10%, red > +10% (expensive).

Example sensitivity bullets (high level):
- Under low utilization (30%), $/1M for a100 in us-east-1 increases ~+40% compared to baseline because tokens_per_gpu_hour halves. Cheaper instance types become more attractive for spiky bursty workloads.
- Under +20% model efficiency (faster kernels / quantization gains), rtx-6000 moves from 0.193 $/1M to ~0.161 $/1M, making mid-tier instances compelling at scale.
- Regional spot windows: if spot can reduce $/GPUh by >50% for >=20% of our capacity, effective blended $/1M drops materially; but reliability constraints increase tail latency risk.

Operational scenarios to evaluate (each row corresponds to a simulation tab in the sheet):
- Conservative reserved-heavy: 70% reserved in primary region, 30% on-demand cross-region failover. Model allocation pins high-throughput models to reserved pool.
- Cost-optimal opportunistic: route non-latency batch to cheapest region/instance given a quality threshold. Use conservative headroom for canary.
- Latency-first hybrid: chat routed to low-latency a100 pockets (lower utilization but higher $/1M), batch/embeddings to quantized pools.

Decision heuristics derived from heatmap:
- If $/1M in fallback region <= baseline + 5% and network RTT delta <= 60ms, prefer fallback for non-chat workloads.
- If utilization for any committed pool falls below 45% for 30 days, downscale reserved profile or reassign workloads (use A/B routing to shift batch).
- Set a threshold: if rtx-6000 $/1M <= a100 $/1M * 0.9, pilot model variant on rtx-6000 for 2 weeks and evaluate quality/regression metrics.

Open questions / caveats:
- Token/sec numbers are system-averages; per-model profiles vary widely. Need per-model perf profiles for accurate mapping (hook to model catalog).
- Network egress and cross-region data transfer costs not modeled here; add delta columns when considering cross-region routing.
- Headroom for cold-starts and auto-scaling transient capacity assumed inside utilization; real tails can require provisioned spare capacity.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering: generate per-model tokens/sec and latency profile export (ticket JIRA-ML-224).
- Finance: provide committed pricing tiers for upcoming contract negotiations for eu-west-1 and asia-southeast-1.
- Product: define workload classification labels for routing (chat/low-latency vs batch/throughput vs embeddings).
- Ops: build a small simulation harness to iterate on the sensitivity matrix and export heatmap CSV for dashboarding.

Appendix: quick-check formulas to copy into sheet cells (Excel/Sheets friendly):
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = tokens_per_sec * 3600 * utilization
- effective_cost = gpu_hour_price * (1 + overhead_fraction)
- cost_per_1M = effective_cost / (tokens_per_gpu_hour / 1000000)

Raw sample numbers for quick paste (CSV style):
region,instance,gpu_hour_price,tokens_per_sec,utilization,overhead_fraction
us-east-1,a100-80,24,45000,0.60,0.08
eu-west-1,a100-80,28,45000,0.60,0.08
us-west-2,rtx-6000,8.5,22000,0.60,0.08
asia-southeast-1,gpu-eq-light,6,15000,0.60,0.08

Notes for reviewers: this is intentionally exploratory and uses rounded example numbers. Replace cloud price inputs with the latest billing/export and model perf with infra-perf team outputs before making capacity commitments.
